form6.note: All quotes matched in the fetched text except two. The Kerala guideline 4(c) quote matched by eye in the stored copy (The CEO Kerala URL reset the connection from the sandbox on 2026-10-09 (www and bare host, HTTP/1.1 and 2). Read instead from the project's stored copy of the same file, data/india/raw/nrc_research/sources/eci_sir_orders_ceokerala.pdf, whose 24.06.2025 pages are scans with no text layer; read by eye at printed pages 5 to 6 (order paras 13 to 15) and 10 to 11 (guidelines 4, 5, 6).) The CEO Karnataka note (24.08.2026) reset the connection again and could not be re-read here; it supports only the ECINet and Form 6A/7/8 details, which the Form 6 PDF on voters.eci.gov.in and rule 8B also support. The plain text is accurate: PN/120 decision iii and para 2, the 01.10.2026 letter para 3, s.23(3) of the 1950 Act (no inclusion after the last date for nominations and before the completion of that election) and the PIB note all say what is claimed. Step 5 was narrower than the sources: Form 8 also covers shifting from another state (guideline 5(e) and order para 15 pair Form 8 with the declaration for shifts from outside the state). Step 5 corrected. Second reading of 16 October 2026: a step added on item (iii) of the ordinary Form 6 declaration, after S.Y. Quraishi's post of 2 October 2026. The Gazette text of S.O. 2802(E) (pages 34 to 36), the Form 6 PDF (Wayback copies of 27.10.2023 and 19.04.2026), ss. 23(1) and 31 of the 1950 Act, the Commission's letter of 01.10.2026 and the Manual on Electoral Rolls (March 2023, para 14.7.4.1) were each read again and the quotes matched. No Commission guidance on how a previously enrolled person should answer item (iii) was found.
steps: Get Form 6 from your booth level officer (BLO), the registration officer's office, voters.eci.gov.in or the ECINet app.
During the revision, attach the declaration that goes with Form 6 for the revision.
Hand it to the BLO or the registration officer, or file it online, and keep the reference number.

Know what the ordinary Form 6 asks you to sign. It is titled “Application Form for New Voters”, and item (iii) of its declaration says “I am applying for inclusion in Electoral Roll for the first time and my name is not included in any Assembly Constituency/ Parliamentary Constituency.” The Commission's letter of 1 October 2026 tells booth level officers to help people who are no longer on the roll apply through Form 6, its Manual on Electoral Rolls of March 2023 says a person no longer on the roll has to apply again through Form 6 as a new elector, and section 23(1) of the 1950 Act lets anyone not on the roll apply. No Commission document found says how a person who was on a roll before should answer item (iii). Section 31 of the 1950 Act punishes only a statement the person knows or believes to be false, or does not believe to be true, with up to one year in prison, a fine or both, and no court ruling or prosecution for signing item (iii) to get back on the roll has been found.
Apply well before an election is called. No name can be added after the last date for nominations until that election is over.
Use Form 8 if you moved house, within the state or from another state, or if your entry has a mistake. Use Form 6A if you live abroad on an Indian passport.

form7.note: Quotes confirmed. Rules 19(1)(b)(ii), 20(2), 21A proviso, s.22 proviso, Form 7 title and judgment para 141 matched in the fetched text; the order para 14 and guideline 5(b) quotes matched by eye in the stored copy (The CEO Kerala URL reset the connection from the sandbox on 2026-10-09 (www and bare host, HTTP/1.1 and 2). Read instead from the project's stored copy of the same file, data/india/raw/nrc_research/sources/eci_sir_orders_ceokerala.pdf, whose 24.06.2025 pages are scans with no text layer; read by eye at printed pages 5 to 6 (order paras 13 to 15) and 10 to 11 (guidelines 4, 5, 6).) One overstatement. The plain text said a hearing is required before a name is struck off 'for being dead'. Section 22's proviso and the proviso to rule 21A both cover only the grounds of having ceased to be ordinarily resident or being otherwise not entitled; deletion of a dead person on the officer's own motion carries no individual hearing under either. A Form 7 objection on any ground does bring a notice in Form 14 and a hearing under rules 19 and 20, and in the SIR para 14 barred any deletion from the draft without an inquiry. The 'speaking order' in guideline 5(b) is for cases where the officer doubts eligibility; judgment para 141 speaks of a reasoned determination at the claims and objections stage generally, so that sentence stands.
form7.plain: Form 7 is the form for objecting to a name on the roll, or to a name proposed to be added. When someone objects to your name, the registration officer has to send you a notice and hear you before deciding. Before deleting a name on the ground that the person has moved away or is not entitled to be on the roll, the officer has to give that person a reasonable chance to be heard. In the revision no entry could be deleted from the draft without an inquiry and a fair chance to be heard, followed by a written order with reasons. If you get a notice, go to the hearing or send the documents asked for, and ask for the order in writing.

appeal.note: Quotes confirmed: s.24 (footnote markers aside), CEO Goa, PIB, judgment para 138 and rule 27(1)(a)-(b) in the fetched text; order para 14 by eye in the stored copy (The CEO Kerala URL reset the connection from the sandbox on 2026-10-09 (www and bare host, HTTP/1.1 and 2). Read instead from the project's stored copy of the same file, data/india/raw/nrc_research/sources/eci_sir_orders_ceokerala.pdf, whose 24.06.2025 pages are scans with no text layer; read by eye at printed pages 5 to 6 (order paras 13 to 15) and 10 to 11 (guidelines 4, 5, 6).) The plain text said 'Chief Electoral Officers' notes on final rolls give 15 days', in the plural, but only CEO Goa's note is cited and read. Corrected to name it. The 15-day limit for the first appeal therefore rests on one CEO's note, as the gaps list already says; step 2 now ties the 15 days to the decision date.
appeal.plain: If the registration officer's decision goes against you, you can appeal to the District Magistrate under section 24 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950. If the District Magistrate's order also goes against you, a second appeal lies to the state's Chief Electoral Officer. The Commission's revision order kept both appeals and gave 30 days from the District Magistrate's order for the second. The Chief Electoral Officer of Goa, in the note on its final roll, gave 15 days from the registration officer's decision for the first.
steps: Get a copy of the registration officer's order.
Write a short appeal to the District Magistrate, signed by you, with the order attached, within 15 days of the registration officer's decision.
If it is turned down, appeal to the Chief Electoral Officer within 30 days of the District Magistrate's order.
Keep copies and receipts of everything you hand in.

supreme_court.note: All eight quotes matched in the fetched orders and judgment (para 186(h) runs across pages 123 and 124). The 14.08.2025 order also directs display at Panchayat Bhavans and Block Development Officers' offices; the 08.09.2025 order says Aadhaar is not proof of citizenship; the 19.01.2026 order covers the logical discrepancy category, authorised representatives and an additional 10 days; the 10.03.2026 order provides for Appellate Tribunals of former Chief Justices and Judges; the 13.04.2026 order holds that a pending appeal gives no right to vote. 'Upheld the revision' fairly states para 186(b) to (e).

helpline_drive.note: All quotes matched (PIB 29.10.2025, PN/120, letter of 01.10.2026). The PIB release also names the Voter Helpline Number 1950. One overstatement: the letter says Booth Level Camps 'shall be organised' but special camps for night shelters, labour colonies and the homeless 'may also be organised'. PN/120 says DEOs will hold help desks or special camps 'as per requirement'. The plain text's last sentence made the special camps mandatory. Corrected.
helpline_drive.plain: You can call the voter helpline on 1950, or the national toll-free number 1800-11-1950 from 8 am to 8 pm, and every complaint is logged on the National Grievance Service Portal. The ECINet app has a Book-a-Call with BLO feature, and complaints can also be emailed to complaints@eci.gov.in. After the revision, the Commission ordered BLOs to compare the roll from before the revision with the present one, visit those missing, and help anyone still eligible fill in Form 6. The lists are to be shared with the parties' booth agents, and booth level camps are to be held. Special camps may also be held for people in night shelters and labour colonies and for the homeless.

legal_aid.note: NALSA quotes matched on nalsa.gov.in/legal-aid/ and the home page (15100). The section 12 list on that page includes women and children, SC/ST members, disabled persons, industrial workmen, victims of mass disaster and others, and persons under a state-set income ceiling; the plain text's list is a fair subset. Section 2(c) covers proceedings before 'any court or other authority or tribunal', which supports applying it to a claim, hearing or appeal. Judgment para 10.12 (spanning pages 13 and 14) and para 100 matched. The Verdictum item is press only and is correctly marked so; it is not used in plain or steps.

writ.note: Quotes confirmed (para 175, para 186(h), and the office report reproducing the 11.11.2025 order in W.P.(C) 1074/2025). The last sentence is not supported. The judgment of 27 May 2026 (2026 INSC 564) lists in its cause title W.P.(C) 640 of 2025 with W.P.(C) 634, 644, 645, 646, 637, 636, 638, 630, 631, 642, 686, 700, 701, 708, 676, 674, 719 and 855 of 2025, all Bihar petitions, and 'these writ petitions' are what para 186(i) disposes of. W.P.(C) 1074 of 2025, in which the request to the High Courts was made, and W.P.(C) 737 of 2025 are not in that list, and the West Bengal matter (diary 64235/2025) carried on with orders to April 2026. Nothing read shows the request withdrawn or the remaining validity cases decided. The source note saying 'the matters were disposed of by the judgment' is corrected for the same reason. The sentence 'That request covered cases on whether the revision was valid' also repeated the one before it. Article 226 is not quoted from a primary text, as gaps says; the statement is ordinary constitutional law and is left in.
writ.plain: An elector can ask the High Court, under Article 226 of the Constitution, to review a decision on the roll. The Supreme Court's judgment of 27 May 2026 says the Commission's enquiry into eligibility remains open to judicial review, and that people in Bihar whose names were, in its words, "erroneously deleted" as absent, dead, shifted or duplicate may challenge the decision that way. On 11 November 2025, while it was hearing the challenges to the revision, the Supreme Court asked the High Courts to hold back cases on whether the revision was valid. That request did not cover an elector's own case about his or her own entry. The judgment of 27 May 2026 decided the petitions about Bihar, and the petition in which the request was made is not among the cases it lists.

It had urged the Chief Electoral Officer's office to reach these women, welcomed the assistance camps held in red-light areas, and asked the Commission to accept documents issued by their cooperative society.
